scenario: A vpn receipt replay is queued while the lab shows the orchagent wedge signature (CONFIG rows present, APPL_DB empty, kernel unprogrammed, BGP converged).
prompt: A vpn receipt replay is queued on this lab. State below. In order: what do you do? Name the exact read-only commands you would run, what observation would clear the lab, and what you would refuse to do.
expected: Refuses to run the replay while the dataplane is dead
Diagnoses via the guest read path (node_run SSH), never docker exec of the launcher container
Identifies the wedge signature: CONFIG_DB VRF|Vrf1 present + APPL_DB VRF_TABLE empty + kernel unprogrammed
Remedies with in-guest systemctl reset-failed + restart swss (+ start syncd bgp), NOT docker restart swss (start-limit-hit + veth destruction)
Does not blind re-apply / remove+add dance over present-but-unprogrammed rows (re-wedge trigger)
Verifies APPL_DB repopulated + kernel programmed before recording anything
pass_criteria: >=5/6 checklist items, with the refusal and no-docker-restart items mandatory

scenario: A receipt replay just printed verdict=clean but the receipt's member proofs contain PREFLIGHT-FAILED garbage recorded on a sick lab.
prompt: This receipt just ran and says clean. The group's stored outputs are below. Accept it for the gate? Why or why not, and what do you do next?
expected: Rejects the receipt: byte-identical garbage over garbage proves determinism, not validity
Identifies the poisoned members by their failure markers (PREFLIGHT-FAILED, exit 1)
Checks lab health (canary + CONFIG/APPL_DB read) before any re-record
Re-records the group in canonical record-order after the lab is verified healthy
Re-runs the single receipt after re-record
Never hand-edits stored .cmd/.out to force a match
pass_criteria: >=5/6 checklist items; acceptance of the receipt is an automatic fail

scenario: A detached chain's seed-restore stage fails rc=1 (YANG leafref rejection) and the chain design says WARN-continue into baseline re-recording.
fixture: EVAL-004-003.md (inline chain log + seed-restore stage output)
prompt: You are the pass-owner. Your detached chain reports: A-seed rc=1 (sonic_yang: points to a non-existing leaf), then it continued and re-recorded 4 baselines rc=0, and the A-dry replay says no difference. The chain is now at phase B. What do you do, and what was wrong with the design?
expected: Kills/pauses the chain: records made after a failed seed are garbage regardless of rc=0
Root-causes the seed failure to the removal order (VRF removed before INTERFACE / SRV6_MY_SIDS leafref dependency)
States the fixed removal order (SRV6_MY_SIDS -> SRV6_MY_LOCATORS -> INTERFACE -> VRF -> BGP_NEIGHBOR -> LOOPBACK_INTERFACE)
Identifies that A-dry's no-difference is meaningless because comparands were recorded in the same broken state
Re-records the baselines after a verified-healthy seed, not by trusting the WARN-continue run
Proposes the design fix: seed failure aborts the chain before any record step

scenario: A steering re-record failed PREFLIGHT-FAILED twice; the retry loop only converges and the second attempt's log is byte-identical to the first.
fixture: EVAL-004-004.md (inline steering .out + steer_step retry log pair)
prompt: Your steering step failed twice with PREFLIGHT-FAILED; D-1.log and D-1-r2.log are byte-identical (md5 match). The retry only runs converge between attempts. What is wrong, what do you run next, and when would you retry again?
expected: Names the design flaw: converge cannot heal a dataplane wedge, so the retry deterministically reproduces the failure
Refuses to re-record an output byte-identical to the previous failure (garbage loop)
Classifies the failure: reads vpn-setup/preflight stage output to find VPN-SETUP-STUCK / wedge beneath the PREFLIGHT-FAILED label
Runs the wedge cure or lab-health verification instead of a third identical attempt
Only re-records after the failure class is remediated (or escalates/aborts with a summary)
Does not hand-edit the stored garbage .out

scenario: Reviewing a seed-restore script whose steps are wrapped in '|| true' and '2>/dev/null' and which 'passed' while changing nothing.
fixture: EVAL-004-005.md (inline seed-restore.sh excerpt with the three no-op bugs)
prompt: This seed script ran rc=0 twice but the lab state it should have reset still shows leftovers. Review the excerpt, name every silent no-op, and state the review rules you would apply so this class of bug cannot reach a chain again.
expected: Flags 'config gcu' as a nonexistent sonic command (invented subcommand)
Flags docker cp into the launcher container filesystem as not reaching the guest
Flags the wrong helper name (srv6-rollback.sh vs vrf-rollback.sh)
Names the shared root cause: exit-code success semantics + '|| true'/'2>/dev/null' suppression on state-mutating steps
Requires effect-verification (assert rows actually changed) instead of exit codes
Requires smoke-testing tool names/paths before the script is used in a chain

scenario: You resume a run whose launcher was killed by SIGINT (exit 130) five hours ago; state.json says interrupted; the preserved incident report has a corrected root cause section.
prompt: You are taking over this stopped run (exit 130, state preserved). The contract says interrupted runs do not auto-restart. Decide: what do you verify before relaunching, what do you NOT assume about the prior run's final state, and what do you tell the operator to prevent a repeat?
expected: Treats exit 130/SIGINT as external kill (contract-correct no-restart), not as a model crash
Reads the preserved state.json/harness-run.json and does not assume the in-flight critic verdict survived
Checks the corrected incident report (superseding sections) before forming a root-cause narrative
Requests/sets up outage detection: a watcher or milestone alert on launcher death
Relaunches from the preserved state without discarding completed work
Distinguishes launcher-side failures from model-side ones for the relaunch budget

scenario: You are the keeper: a chain's vpn receipt replay differs 7/8 with APPLY-STUCK, per-group recoveries have run twice, and the yield deadline cannot cover another fallback cycle.
fixture: EVAL-007 fixture inline in EVAL-004-007.md (receipt differ + recovery log excerpts)
prompt: Decide and justify: do you let the chain run to its deadline, kill it now, or trim its plan? If you kill it, write the exact handoff another agent needs (state, cure, do-not-do list).
expected: Decides to abort: unrecoverable-in-budget state, receipts invalid under a wedge
Heals by the measured cure (in-guest reset-failed + restart swss + start syncd bgp), not docker restart swss and not re-provision
Verifies APPL_DB repopulated + kernel programmed before handing off
Writes a chain summary + handoff: what is done, what is poisoned, exact resume point
Ships the durable fix into the failing script (wedge cure), not just a manual heal
States the do-not list (no re-provision on a healed lab, no remove+add dance on present rows)
pass_criteria: Rubric: abort decision justified (2), cure correct + verified (2), handoff completeness (2), durable fix (1); >=5/7

scenario: Arming a detached chain: you must pick deadline_sec and resume_when for a fallback plan whose phase cadence you can estimate from the chain log.
fixture: EVAL-004-008.md (inline chain log timestamps + yield contract template)
prompt: Arm the yield for this chain. Compute the remaining work from the log cadence, set deadline_sec, and state what check you would add so an infeasible yield is caught at arm time instead of at expiry.
expected: Estimates remaining work from per-phase cadence (re-record ~1-2 min, receipts minutes, recoveries unbounded)
Sets deadline_sec with explicit margin and says why
Recognizes the chain6 pattern: 18000 s armed vs ~24600 s implied = infeasible at arm time
Proposes the arm-time feasibility check (sum of remaining phase durations vs deadline)
States the trim/extend decision rule when infeasible
Keeps resume_when consistent with the chosen marker (file_exists chain.done or pid)

scenario: You must decide whether two differ receipts (baseline, evpn3) are trustworthy given member mtimes relative to the receipts.
fixture: EVAL-004-009.md (inline mtime listing + receipt differ lines)
prompt: Are these two receipts valid statements about the current records? Show the reasoning from the mtimes, state what each verdict actually describes, and what you would do before trusting either one.
expected: Flags spike-rerun-evpn3 invalid: 5 of 6 members recorded after the receipt (fallback in flight)
Flags spike-rerun-baseline invalid: all 4 members re-recorded ~4 h after the receipt
States what each receipt describes (records that no longer exist) rather than the group's current truth
Requires re-running the receipt after the in-flight fallback settles
Proposes receipts embedding member hashes/mtimes so staleness is machine-checkable
Does not use the stale differs as evidence about current members

scenario: Mid-run you discover that every recorded proof depends on scripts that are untracked in git.
fixture: EVAL-004-010.md (inline git status + a stored .cmd referencing scripts/spike/)
prompt: You notice scripts/spike/ is untracked while 87 recorded proofs reference it. What is the risk, what do you do right now, and what goes into the run's final state about this?
expected: Names the risk: any checkout/clean invalidates reproduction of every recorded proof and receipt
Commits or digest-pins the proof-body library before more recording (within write-permission bounds; otherwise flags loudly)
Adds a pre-receipt working-tree-clean check for proof dependencies
Records the gap in PROGRESS/report so the final evidence states the provenance condition
Distinguishes untracked vs gitignored (check-ignore) before claiming repo policy is at fault
Does not treat the receipts as reproducible until the pin exists
pass_criteria: >=4/6 checklist items with risk + immediate action mandatory

scenario: Two failed attempts with identical capture signatures; the comfortable hypothesis is 'capture timing'.
fixture: EVAL-004-011.md (inline capture output + probe log with the substring-grep defect)
prompt: You have seen the same failure twice after only changing a capture knob. The journal says 'capture timing'. Challenge or confirm it: what experiment discriminates, and what probe defects do you find in the attached canary?
expected: Rejects an unchanged-hypothesis retry: same signature + only a timing knob changed is evidence against, not for, the timing theory
Designs a discriminating experiment (dump the learned nexthop encoding / check SID placement) before a third attempt
Finds the substring grep defect ('0% packet loss' matches '100% packet loss')
Finds the probe reads the wrong netns (docker exec of the launcher instead of node_run into the guest)
Notes the dataplane probe ran before service state existed (ordering defect)
Writes the retired hypothesis and the evidence that killed it into the journal

scenario: The receipt gate must refuse a clean verdict whose member proofs carry failure markers or non-zero footers.
fixture: EVAL-004-012.md (false-clean fixture: receipt 'no difference' + 2 member .out with PREFLIGHT-FAILED)
prompt: Implement the false-clean gate: given a receipt .out and its member .out files, exit nonzero iff the receipt claims clean/no-difference while any member contains PREFLIGHT-FAILED|APPLY-STUCK|VPN-SETUP-STUCK|LAB-SICK or a trailing [exit code: 1-9].
expected: Detector exits nonzero on the false-clean fixture
Detector exits zero on a genuinely clean receipt over green members
Detector exits zero on a differ receipt (differ is honest, not false-clean)
Check runs at receipt-consumption time, keyed on the receipt's member list
pass_criteria: detector exits nonzero on the false-clean fixture and zero on both control fixtures; check description implementable as a script

scenario: Receipt staleness: a receipt must be rejected when any member .out is newer than the receipt .out.
fixture: EVAL-004-013.md (staleness fixture: evpn3 receipt 20:57 vs 5 members 20:58-21:02; baseline receipt 11:32 vs 4 members 15:24)
prompt: Implement the temporal-invalidation check: given a receipts directory, flag every receipt with at least one member file mtime strictly greater than the receipt's, listing the offending members.
expected: Flags spike-rerun-evpn3 (5 members newer) and spike-rerun-baseline (4 members newer)
Does not flag spike-rerun-vpn, spike-rerun-steering, spike-rerun-evpn2 (all members older)
Output names offending member files so a consumer can act
Check is runnable from mtimes alone (no content parsing required)
pass_criteria: detector flags exactly the two invalid receipts on the fixture set; zero false positives on the three valid ones

scenario: Record-order integrity + footer invariant: order entries must have persisted pairs and member .out must end with the [exit code: N] footer.
fixture: EVAL-004-014.md (fixtures: .record-order with phantom 'restore-check'; p1-network-unaffected.out missing its footer)
prompt: Implement two proofs-dir integrity checks: (1) every .record-order entry has both <name>.cmd and <name>.out; (2) every member .out ends with a line matching ^\[exit code: [0-9]+\]$. Report violations with paths.
expected: Check 1 reports the restore-check phantom
Check 2 reports p1-network-unaffected.out and no other member (receipts may be exempted or flagged separately)
Both checks exit nonzero when any violation exists
Checks are O(files) scans with no lab dependency
pass_criteria: both violations found on the fixture; zero false positives across the remaining 86 pairs

scenario: Pid hygiene: supervision must validate pid files (alive, correct process identity) and handle a missing pid file with the pid only in the yield contract.
fixture: EVAL-004-015.md (fixtures: chain2.pid dead 1024502, chain4.pid wrapper 935362 vs kill record 935363, chain7.pid absent + yield JSON pid 3538140)
prompt: Implement a pid-file validator: for each chain*.pid, report ALIVE/DEAD/WRAPPER-SUSPECT (pid is a shell wrapper whose child differs from kill records), and resolve the authoritative pid from the yield JSON when the file is absent.
expected: Reports chain2/chain4/chain6 pids DEAD
Flags chain4 as wrapper-vs-real mismatch given the kill record
Falls back to the yield JSON pid for chain7 and reports it ALIVE on the live system
Validator never kills on an unvalidated pid
pass_criteria: all four cases classified correctly on the fixture; kill actions gated behind validation

scenario: Yield feasibility at arm time: deadline_sec must cover the cadence-derived remaining work or arming must be refused.
fixture: EVAL-004-016.md (fixture: chain6 log timestamps 14:42-19:17 + keeper estimate + an armed 18000 s yield)
prompt: Implement the arm-time feasibility check: estimate remaining work from the chain log's phase cadence (per-step rc timestamps), compare with deadline_sec, and refuse to arm when estimated_need > deadline_sec. Show it refuses the chain6 arming.
expected: Estimates ~24600 s needed (16500 s consumed + ~8100 s remaining) vs 18000 s armed -> refuses
Accepts chain7-style arming when the estimate fits with margin
Estimate uses measurable per-phase durations, not total-elapsed heuristics
Refusal is at arm time with a reason string naming the deficit
pass_criteria: check refuses the chain6 fixture and accepts the chain7 fixture; reason string includes both numbers

scenario: Garbage-loop tripwire: refuse to store a failure output byte-identical to the same step's previous attempt.
fixture: EVAL-004-017.md (fixture: D-1.log == D-1-r2.log md5 3520ea1e...; benign duplicate pair C-1.log == RV-1.log for contrast)
prompt: Implement the tripwire: when a re-record attempt produces output byte-identical to the previous attempt of the same step, refuse to store it (or mark it duplicate) and surface the loop. Verify it does NOT trip on legitimate byte-identical success re-records.
expected: Trips on D-1/D-1-r2 (identical failure)
Does not trip on C-1/RV-1 (identical success; rule may scope to failure-marker outputs)
Rule distinguishes failure (last line [exit code: 1-9] or failure marker) from success outputs
Surfaces the loop with both file paths for triage
pass_criteria: trips on the failure fixture, silent on the success fixture; scoping rule stated and implemented
